The failure physics involves particle kinetic energy transfer: the graded interface converts impact energy to elastic deformation, reducing stress on the substrate below the fatigue threshold.

PHYSICS CHECK — Governing relation: Energy absorption by viscoelastic layer (1/2 * k * δ² = E_impact), where k is effective stiffness, δ is maximum deflection. For a 10 mm thick polyurethane layer (k ~ 50 MPa), absorbing a 1 J impact (typical for 2 mm steel particle at 30 m/s), δ = sqrt(2*1/50e6) = 6.3 mm — feasible within the layer thickness. Deflection magnitude is CALCULATED from impact energy and material modulus (stated physics).

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — Components: (1) Primary structure (existing elbow material, ALREADY-RECORDED per problem geometry); (2) Graded modulus interface: 5 mm Shore A 95 polyurethane (abrasion-resistant layer) bonded to 5 mm Shore A 70 polyurethane (energy-absorbing layer); (3) Replaceable outer shell: 3 mm UHMW-PE (low-friction sacrificial layer). Materials: Polyurethane (graded modulus, ALREADY-RECORDED per elastomer coating precedent), UHMW-PE (abrasion-resistant, ALREADY-RECORDED per slurry pump liner precedent). Maintenance: Shell replacement every 6 months (CALCULATED from stated wear rate: 0.5 mm/month), same as standard liner replacement frequency, SAME burden. Pass/fail threshold: Shell thickness must not drop below 1 mm within 6 months (CALCULATED from stated wear rate). Duration: 6 months.
